goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 + app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 + app/models/post.rb:131 — Imported external HTML is stored with cook_method: raw_html (Post#cook returns raw completely unsanitized) and rendered via raw post.cooked; the PollFeed path applies no tag/attribute filtering (unlike the readability path), so <script>/onerror in feed content becomes stored XSS on the forum origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a raw-HTML cooking path: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` while passing `contents` from the feed through `absolutize_urls` but not sanitizing/filtering tags/attributes (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The scheduled `PollFeed` job imports `i.content` from RSS/ATOM into `TopicEmbed.import` with no whitelist or sanitization (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). The embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any `<script>`/event-handler HTML in feed content would be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS on the forum origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:12 — "#{url}" interpolates the unescaped URL into HTML; only the scheme is validated, so a feed link like http://host/a' onmouseover='alert(1) breaks out of the attribute → stored XSS in every imported post

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code appends HTML containing an tag built via string interpolation: `"#{url}"`. The only validation shown is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which would still allow single quotes or other attribute-breaking characters in `url` (e.g. `http://host/a' onmouseover='alert(1)`). Since imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and Post#cook returns `raw` for raw_html, this HTML is stored/rendered without the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (and embed view uses `raw post.cooked`). That makes the described stored XSS attack verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:25 — The only gate is the Referer header, which is trivially spoofed; every /embed/best request with a novel embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job that may synchronously run a full PollFeed plus an outbound fetch — unauthenticated job-queue flooding / fetch amplification (the 60s redis throttle is per-URL, so unique URLs bypass it)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a publicly reachable `GET /embed/best` route that, when no existing embed is found, unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` (EmbedController#best). Access control in `ensure_embeddable` relies solely on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which is not a strong/authenticated signal and can be spoofed by non-browser clients. Once enqueued, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, whose throttling is keyed by the full `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so attackers can bypass it by varying URLs on the allowed host. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` may synchronously run `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` and then does outbound `open(url)` fetches (both in PollFeed and TopicEmbed.import_remote), creating job-queue flooding and fetch amplification potential. This is a real security/DoS risk introduced by the new embed feature as shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url) follows redirects without re-validating the host, so a page on embeddable_host can redirect to internal endpoints (SSRF) and the fetched content is then published on the forum

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the code does `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no redirect limit/validation. Although `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` before calling `import_remote`, that check only validates the *initial* URL. `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects by default, so an attacker-controlled page on the allowed `embeddable_host` could redirect to an internal/metadata endpoint, causing SSRF and then publishing the fetched content via `TopicEmbed.import(...)` (ultimately stored as raw HTML). This risk is directly grounded in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 / app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 — open(...) is called with no timeout or response-size limit; a slow remote server hangs the Sidekiq job indefinitely and a huge response can OOM the process

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetches using Ruby's open-uri without any explicit timeout or response-size limit: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30` and `open(url).read` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb:48` (`import_remote`). As written, these can block indefinitely on slow/unresponsive servers and can read arbitrarily large bodies into memory (especially `open(url).read`), potentially hanging Sidekiq workers or causing OOM.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] config (missing from diff) — embed.js and embed.css are new standalone top-level bundles but are never added to config.assets.precompile, so they will 404 in production unless the precompile list is glob-based; verify registration in config/application.rb

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add new standalone assets (`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`) and references `embed` via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, but the finding asserts they are “never added to config.assets.precompile” and will 404 in production. No asset precompile configuration (`config/application.rb`, initializers, etc.) is shown in the diff, so we can’t verify whether Discourse already precompiles all manifests/globs or explicitly includes `embed`. Therefore the claim isn’t verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:7 — t.string :embed_url yields varchar(255); URLs longer than 255 chars (common with tracking params) fail on insert with 'value too long', and skip_validations: true means no length validation catches it first → import/job errors

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the column is defined as `t.string :embed_url`, which in Rails maps to `varchar(255)` by default. The code later persists arbitrary external URLs (e.g., RSS `i.link` / `i.id`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` inputs) via `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` without any length validation in the model. If an embed URL exceeds 255 characters, the insert/update can fail at the DB level and break feed import / retrieval jobs. This limitation is introduced by the diff and can cause real runtime errors for some valid URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb / spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb — Nothing tests the security-critical import path: no spec feeds hostile HTML (script tags, event handlers, javascript: hrefs) through TopicEmbed.import/PollFeed#poll_feed to assert sanitization, and poll_feed_spec only stubs poll_feed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an import path that explicitly bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`. In the embed UI, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders `raw post.cooked`, so any hostile HTML in RSS/remote content can be served directly. The finding’s point that there are no specs feeding hostile HTML through `TopicEmbed.import` / `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` to assert sanitization is grounded, and it corresponds to a real security defect exposed by this diff (not merely a test preference).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] app/models/topic_embed.rb:14-27 — Check-then-insert race on embed_url between concurrent PollFeed and RetrieveTopic runs; the unique index raises an unhandled RecordNotUnique, killing the job (and with retry: false, the rest of the feed run)

adjudication.rationale: TopicEmbed.import does a non-atomic check-then-insert on embed_url: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` when `embed.blank?` (inside a transaction, but without locking). With the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` added in the migration, concurrent callers (e.g., PollFeed iterating feeds and RetrieveTopic/TopicRetriever importing the same URL) can both observe no row and then one will raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique. There is no rescue/handling around `create!` in TopicEmbed.import or in Jobs::PollFeed (which also sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`), so the exception can kill the job and stop the rest of the feed loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] lib/topic_retriever.rb:30-33 — $redis.setnx followed by $redis.expire is not atomic; a crash between the two leaves the key with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed_url; use SET key 1 EX 60 NX

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb (retrieved_recently?), throttling uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This two-step pattern is non-atomic; if the process crashes or errors after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key will remain without a TTL and `retrieved_recently?` will return true forever for that embed_url, effectively permanently throttling retrieval. The finding’s suggested atomic `SET ... NX EX 60` would avoid this defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:9 — No null check on document.getElementById('discourse-comments'); a TypeError is thrown on any page where the placeholder div is missing

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is assigned from `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally used via `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the element is missing, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a `TypeError`. The diff shows no guard/check before use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8 — Reloads every 30s forever; if retrieval permanently fails (fetch error, host mismatch, missing embed user) the iframe polls indefinitely with no terminal state

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` the page unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` after 30s with no stop condition. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it always renders `loading` and enqueues `:retrieve_topic`; if retrieval never succeeds (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` user is blank, or remote fetch/import fails), `topic_id` will remain nil and the iframe will keep reloading indefinitely with no terminal error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/models/topic_embed.rb:38 — If the imported post/topic was deleted, the orphaned TopicEmbed row leaves embed.post nil and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError, aborting the poll run

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing TopicEmbed is found, it does `post = embed.post` and (if the SHA1 changed) unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!` (app/models/topic_embed.rb, else branch). If the referenced Post was deleted, `embed.post` will be nil (no FK/dependent cleanup shown in the diff), so `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise (and abort the PollFeed run that iterates items). There is no nil-check/cleanup for this orphaned state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 / app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — doc.title / i.title can be nil; combined with skip_validations: true this creates topics with blank/nil titles

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, TopicEmbed.import_remote uses `opts[:title] || doc.title` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) and PollFeed passes `i.title` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). Both `doc.title` and `i.title` can be nil for some pages/feeds. TopicEmbed.import then calls `PostCreator.new(... title: title, ..., skip_validations: true, ...)`, so a nil/blank title can flow into topic/post creation while validations are explicitly skipped, making it possible to create topics with blank titles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 — The --category option is removed outright with no deprecation or migration note, silently breaking existing invocations of the import task

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the logic that read `options[:category]` to choose a category_id. The import path now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` without any category parameter. This is a real, diff-grounded backward-incompatible CLI/API change that would break existing scripts invoking `disqus:import --category ...`, but it’s not inherently a correctness defect if the change is intentional—it's a compatibility/documentation/deprecation concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4 — Modifies an already-shipped migration to add force: true (plus whitespace/newline churn in migrate_word_counts); editing historical migrations is unsafe — force: true would drop existing top_topics data anywhere the migration had not yet been recorded

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails migrations, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can cause data loss if this migration is executed against a DB where `top_topics` exists but the migration isn’t recorded as run. This is a real, diff-grounded safety/correctness risk (separate from the whitespace/newline churn noted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:18 — feed_key (and the require 'digest/sha1') is dead code, never referenced anywhere in the diff

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `require 'digest/sha1'` is only used by the `feed_key` method, and `feed_key` is not referenced anywhere in this diff (execute only calls `poll_feed`; `poll_feed` parses RSS and calls `TopicEmbed.import`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:25 / lib/topic_retriever.rb:16 — embeddable_host is compared verbatim against URI(...).host (which is downcased/stripped of scheme); an admin entering 'https://Blog.Example.com' or mixed case silently breaks both the referer check and retrieval with no validation warning

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds host checks that do a strict string comparison between `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and `URI(...).host` (EmbedController `ensure_embeddable`: `URI(request.referer||'').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; TopicRetriever `invalid_host?`: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). `URI(...).host` returns only the hostname (no scheme) and is normalized to lowercase, while the site setting is an arbitrary string with no validation/normalization in this diff. If an admin enters a value like `https://Blog.Example.com` or mixed case, the comparisons will fail, breaking embedding/retrieval as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — The snippet silently requires discourseUrl to end with '/' (otherwise the src becomes 'forum.comembed/best'); this contract is undocumented for integrators

adjudication.rationale: In newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the iframe URL is constructed via string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. There is no normalization to ensure `discourseUrl` ends with `/`, so an integrator-provided value like `https://forum.example.com` would produce `https://forum.example.comembed/best...`, breaking the embed. The diff shows no documentation or guard for this contract.
